nodes.content: Design a persistent-memory transactional index combining serializable concurrency, crash-safe memory reclamation, and recovery independent of total index size.
requirements: Recover after every injected persistence-boundary crash without losing acknowledged commits or resurrecting reclaimed records.
Recovery reads at most 64 MiB per 100 GiB index, independent of completed transaction count.

nodes.content: Use serializable optimistic validation, copy-on-write roots, dual 8 MiB commit manifests, and lazily loaded generation-tagged free maps.
How can manifest publication atomically link committed roots to free-map generations across crashes without scanning historical transactions?
Flushing root/free-map generations before publishing a checksummed inactive manifest preserves acknowledged commits without resurrection, using ≤16 MiB recovery reads.
Run BoundaryCrash-1 on 100 GiB images, crashing after each root, free-map, and manifest flush; verify commits, reclamation, recovery bytes.
BoundaryCrash-1: 12,480 crashes caused zero lost acknowledged commits or resurrected records; recovery read at most 16 MiB per 100 GiB.
Adopt ordered root/free-map flushes and checksummed inactive-manifest publication; BoundaryCrash-1 verified crash safety with 16 MiB recovery reads.
Implement adopted manifest publication with predicate-version validation and epoch-gated reclamation; crash-test 10 million transactions against the 64 MiB recovery cap.
Build IndexProto-1 with dual-manifest publication, predicate-version validation, and epoch-gated reclamation; inject crashes during 10 million transactions.
IndexProto-1 contains predicate-versioned transactions, copy-on-write roots, epoch-gated free maps, dual-manifest commits, and a 10-million-transaction crash-injection harness.
Fault IndexProto-1 at every flush across 10 million transactions; check serializability, acknowledged commits, freed-record absence, and recovery reads.
IndexProto-1’s 10-million-transaction fault run found zero serializability violations, lost acknowledged commits, or resurrected records; recovery read ≤16 MiB/100 GiB.
An aligned 8-byte durable selector to an immutable root/free-map capsule permits ≤8 KiB recovery reads without history scans.
Test selector publication in SelectorCrash-1, crashing at each flush across 10 million transactions; measure recovery bytes and reclamation safety.
SelectorCrash-1 found two stale-pointer resurrections without generation scans; preventing them required 24 MiB recovery reads, exceeding 8 KiB.
A durable selector plus generation-stamped pointers and free-map summaries prevents resurrection without history scans, reading ≤32 MiB.
Rerun SelectorCrash-1 with generation-stamped pointers and free-map summaries, checking stale-pointer resurrection and recovery reads against 32 MiB.
SelectorCrash-1 retest found zero resurrected records or lost acknowledged commits across 10 million transactions; summary-only recovery read 28 MiB/100 GiB.
How does optimistic validation detect range-scan phantoms across copy-on-write leaf splits without scanning the entire index?
Add fence-interval version stamps to scans, validate under the commit latch, then test concurrent inserts and splits for phantoms.
Run PhantomSplit-1 with 32 concurrent scanners and inserters, forcing leaf splits; compare committed histories against a serializability oracle.
PhantomSplit-1 bundle contains 32-worker leaf-split schedules, fence-version validation traces, committed histories, and serializability-oracle reports.
PhantomSplit-1 checked 2 million committed transactions under 32 workers: zero serializability violations; validation read no unrelated leaves.
Use strict two-phase predicate locks, shadow-paged roots, and a 16 MiB double-buffered allocation directory with epoch-quarantined reuse.
How can the bounded allocation directory track epoch-quarantined reuse through sustained churn without replaying completed transactions?
Publishing quarantine-ring checkpoints with shadow roots before slot reuse should keep recovery ≤32 MiB/100 GiB after 100 million transactions.
Extend PhantomSplit-1 schedules to 100 million split/delete/reuse transactions; crash at checkpoint and reuse flushes, checking resurrection and ≤32 MiB recovery.
Extended PhantomSplit-1: 100 million transactions yielded zero resurrections or lost acknowledged commits; worst-case recovery read 32 MiB/100 GiB.
Choose checkpointed quarantine-ring reclamation for high churn: 100-million-transaction coverage at 32 MiB outweighs selector’s 28 MiB over 10 million.
Implement chosen quarantine-ring checkpoint rollover in the 16 MiB directory; test billion-transaction churn for safe reuse and ≤32 MiB recovery.
Run RingChurn-1 for one billion delete/reuse transactions, crashing at rollover flushes and measuring resurrection count and recovery bytes.
RingChurn-1 bundle records billion-transaction delete/reuse histories, rollover crash images, reclaimed-slot checks, and recovery-read measurements.
Audit RingChurn-1 crash images and replay its histories on IndexProto-1; compare commit loss, resurrections, serializability, and recovery reads.
Billion-transaction RingChurn-1: both designs had zero lost commits, resurrections, or serializability failures; p2 read 32 MiB/100 GiB.
Replay PhantomSplit-1’s 32-worker schedules through billion-transaction churn, comparing p2 checkpoint rollover with p1 reclamation for reuse safety and recovery reads.
Combined PhantomSplit-1/churn replay exposed 17 p2 phantom commits during leaf splits despite predicate locks; p1 had zero.
Select p1: p2 passed churn recovery but produced 17 split phantoms; p1 had zero violations and 16 MiB/100 GiB recovery.
Per-extent epoch-stamped quarantine bitmaps checkpointed with shadow roots prevent resurrection through one billion reuses with ≤32 MiB recovery reads.
Run BitmapCrash-1 across one billion reuse operations, injecting crashes at bitmap and root checkpoints; measure resurrections and recovery reads.
BitmapCrash-1’s billion-reuse run found three reclaimed-slot resurrections; bitmap replay prevented them but raised recovery reads to 48 MiB/100 GiB.
Which bitmap checkpoint ordering prevents the three reclaimed-slot resurrections without requiring 48 MiB of replay?
Test bitmap-before-root persistence and post-checkpoint reuse on BitmapCrash-1’s three failing schedules; measure resurrections and ≤32 MiB recovery.
Bitmap-before-root flushes and post-checkpoint reuse eliminated all three resurrections; recovery read 30 MiB/100 GiB on those schedules.
Combine fence-version validation with bitmap-before-root checkpoints, post-checkpoint reuse, and dual 24 MiB extent directories.
Implement p3; crash-test billion-transaction split/reuse workloads at every flush, checking serializability, acknowledged commits, resurrection, and ≤64 MiB/100 GiB recovery.
Integrate PhantomSplit-1 schedules into P3Crash-1; crash billion-transaction split/reuse runs at every bitmap, root, and directory flush.
P3Crash-1 contains billion-transaction split/reuse histories, persistence-boundary crash images, serializability traces, reclaimed-slot checks, and recovery-byte logs.
Audit P3Crash-1 for lost commits, serializability violations, and resurrections; verify ≤64 MiB/100 GiB recovery after million and billion transactions.
P3Crash-1: zero acknowledged-commit losses, resurrections, or serializability violations over one billion transactions; recovery read ≤48 MiB/100 GiB at both scales.
Adopt p3: fence-version validation avoids split phantoms, while billion-transaction crash tests show zero failures and ≤48 MiB/100 GiB recovery.
Replace exploratory testing with release hardening: enforce root-publication acknowledgement barriers, verify directory rollover, and document 48 MiB recovery bound.
Run ReleaseGate-1 across acknowledgement and directory-rollover flushes; audit published-root barriers, reclaimed slots, and recovery-read limits.
ReleaseGate-1 extends P3Crash-1 with acknowledgement-barrier and directory-rollover crash images, reclaimed-slot audits, and recovery-byte logs.
Run ScaleCrash-1 on 100 GiB and 1 TiB p3 indexes; crash rollovers after million/billion commits, measuring recovery reads.
ScaleCrash-1: 1 TiB recovery rose from 480 to 768 MiB across million/billion commits, exceeding 64 MiB/100 GiB.
Checkpoint rollover deltas into per-extent directories before root publication, keeping 1 TiB recovery ≤480 MiB after billion commits.
Extend ReleaseGate-1 with prepublication rollover-delta checkpoints; crash 1 TiB indexes after billion commits, checking reclamation and ≤480 MiB recovery.
Extended ReleaseGate-1: zero lost commits or resurrections after billion commits; 1 TiB recovery read 472 MiB with prepublication checkpoints.
Reinstate p3 with prepublication rollover checkpoints: billion-commit recovery read 472 MiB/1 TiB without lost commits or resurrections.
How do dual extent directories identify the latest complete bitmap checkpoint after a crash interrupts rollover?
CRC-protected generation headers and an atomic root epoch select the newest complete directory, discarding interrupted rollover checkpoints.
Extend ReleaseGate-1 with crashes at CRC-header and root-epoch flushes; verify complete-directory selection, acknowledged commits, and reclaimed-slot absence.
ReleaseGate-1 CRC/epoch crashes selected the latest complete directory in 8,192 cases, with zero lost commits or resurrections.
Finalize reinstated p3 with CRC/epoch directory selection: 8,192 rollover crashes passed, 472 MiB/1 TiB recovery, versus p2’s 17 phantoms.
